stops.title: Linear S.H.M. and differential equation
stops.inShort: In linear S.H.M., restoring force F = −kx is directly proportional to displacement x from mean position and directed towards it. Differential equation: d²x/dt² + ω²x = 0 where ω² = k/m.

stops.title: Displacement, velocity, acceleration & phase
stops.inShort: x = A sin(ωt + φ), v = ±ω√(A² − x²), a = −ω²x. Velocity is maximum (Aω) at mean position; acceleration is maximum (Aω²) at extreme positions.

stops.title: Energy in S.H.M. & composition of two S.H.M.s
stops.inShort: KE = ½ m ω²(A² − x²), PE = ½ m ω² x², Total energy E = ½ m ω² A² = ½ k A² (constant). Resultant amplitude of two collinear S.H.M.s of same period: R = √(A₁² + A₂² + 2A₁A₂ cos(φ₁−φ₂)).
sections: 5.11 Energy of a Particle Performing S.H.M.

stops.title: Simple pendulum & seconds pendulum
stops.inShort: Period of simple pendulum T = 2π √(L/g) for small amplitude. A seconds pendulum has T = 2 s (length ≈ 0.994 m at g = 9.8 m/s²).

stops.title: Angular S.H.M., damped & forced oscillations
stops.inShort: Period of bar magnet in uniform magnetic field: T = 2π √(I / μB). Damped oscillations decay exponentially due to resistive forces. Resonance occurs when driving frequency equals natural frequency.

items.f: E = KE + PE = (1/2) m ω² A² = (1/2) k A²

items.s: I is moment of inertia; μ is magnetic dipole moment.

board.text: A body of mass 0.8 kg performs linear S.H.M. It experiences a restoring force of 0.4 N, when its displacement from mean position is 4 cm. Determine Force constant and Period of S.H.M.
Obtain an expression for the period of a bar magnet vibrating in a uniform magnetic field, performing S.H.M.
board.answer:
When a bar magnet of magnetic moment μ is deflected by small angle θ in uniform magnetic field B, restoring torque is:
τ = −μ B sin θ ≈ −μ B θ (for small θ).
Also τ = I α = I (d²θ/dt²).
Thus I (d²θ/dt²) + μ B θ = 0 ⇒ d²θ/dt² + (μB/I) θ = 0.
Comparing with d²θ/dt² + ω²θ = 0, ω = √(μB/I).
Period T = 2π/ω = 2π √(I / μB).

points.text: Restoring torque τ = −μB sin θ ≈ −μB θ

board.text: A bar magnet of mass 120 g in the form of a rectangular parallelepiped has dimensions l = 40 mm, b = 10 mm and h = 80 mm with its dimension 'h' vertical; the magnet performs angular oscillations in the plane of the magnetic field with period π seconds. If the magnetic moment is 3.4 A·m², determine the influencing magnetic field.

points.text: Moment of inertia I = m(l² + b²)/12 = 1.7 × 10⁻⁵ kg·m²

board.text: Define linear S.H.M. and obtain its differential equation.
board.answer:
Linear S.H.M. is the linear periodic motion of a body in which the restoring force (or acceleration) is always directed towards the mean position and its magnitude is directly proportional to the displacement from the mean position.
F = −kx. By Newton's 2nd law, m(d²x/dt²) = −kx ⇒ d²x/dt² + (k/m)x = 0.
Putting k/m = ω², we get d²x/dt² + ω²x = 0.

board.text: Derive an expression for the period of a simple pendulum.
board.answer:
For a bob of mass m suspended by a string of length L deflected by small angle θ:
Restoring force F = −mg sin θ ≈ −mg θ = −mg (x/L).
Acceleration a = F/m = −(g/L) x = −ω² x.
Thus ω = √(g/L).
Period T = 2π/ω = 2π √(L/g).
